description: Nickel is a chemical element with symbol Ni and atomic number 28. It is a silvery-white lustrous metal with a slight golden tinge that is hard and ductile. Pure nickel is chemically reactive but forms a passivation layer of nickel oxide on its surface that prevents further corrosion.
uses: About 68% of world production is used in stainless steel, with a further 10% used for nickel-based and copper-based alloys, 9% for plating, 7% for alloy steels, and 3% in foundries. Nickel is also used in coins, rechargeable batteries including those in electric vehicles, as a catalyst for hydrogenation, cathodes for batteries, pigments, and metal surface treatments.
characteristics: Nickel is one of only four elements that are ferromagnetic at or near room temperature, with a Curie temperature of 355°C. It is hard, malleable, and ductile with relatively high electrical and thermal conductivity for transition metals, has a face-centered cubic crystal structure, and can take a high polish.
